official.application_cycle: 2027 New Zealand Space Scholarship - applications opened 1 October 2026, internship runs July to September 2027
official.status_note: The official MBIE page (last updated 01 October 2026) states applications for the 2027 New Zealand Space Scholarship open on 1 October 2026, and MBIE's job application portal (requisition 20205, posted 25/09/2026) states the deadline for applications is Sunday, 1 November 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: No tuition fees are covered: this is a fully supported 3-month internship placement, not a degree award. The official page states: 'The scholarship covers: Return economy flights to the United States; Accommodation; Daily living allowance; Reasonable travel-related expenses, including insurance support where applicable. The scholarship only covers costs associated with participating in the internship. Any additional expenses remain the responsibility of the recipient.' The application portal adds that 'Flights, accommodation, a financial contribution toward other travel costs, and a daily allowance will be provided by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) through the New Zealand Space Scholarship.' No monetary value is published for any component.
benefits: Return economy flights to the United States
Reasonable travel-related expenses, including insurance support where applicable
Hands-on experience on cutting-edge space missions and science projects, working alongside scientists and engineers at JPL
Skills and networks that support future careers in New Zealand's space and advanced aviation sectors, plus representing New Zealand through outreach and engagement activities
eligibility: Be a New Zealand citizen (NASA requirement)

Be enrolled in a postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution in a field relevant to NASA's mission priorities (the portal describes the fields as science, engineering, technology, mathematics or computer science at postgraduate level in 2027, with an interest in space science, engineering or technology)
Hold a minimum GPA equivalent of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (New Zealand grades must be converted to the US GPA scale)
Be proficient in written and spoken English (NASA requirement)
Be available to undertake the internship in person from July to September 2027 (dates subject to change)
Be willing to undergo any required health and security checks for travel to the United States and entry into US federal facilities
Be eligible for a J1 or F1 visa and understand the applicable visa conditions
Be able to obtain appropriate travel and medical insurance
People who currently hold, or have previously held, citizenship in a country listed on NASA's Designated Countries List are not eligible to apply

Students completing their current qualification before 2027 may still apply if they intend to enrol in postgraduate study at a New Zealand tertiary institution and can provide proof of enrolment before the scholarship is awarded
requirements: Applications must be submitted via the Ministry's online job application portal; the New Zealand Space Agency at MBIE is the only official entity able to accept applications for consideration by JPL
Applicants are asked to nominate up to 2 research areas that best match their studies
Candidates must have a high academic standing and meet the scholarship's eligibility requirements
Late or incomplete applications may not be considered
Successful recipients must follow the participant code of conduct, arrange appropriate travel and medical insurance, and participate in promotional, outreach and alumni activities
selection_criteria: Relevance of experience to JPL projects
Commitment to contributing to JPL and New Zealand's space sector
coverage: Return economy flights to the United States
Reasonable travel-related expenses, including insurance support where applicable
application_method: Apply online through MBIE's online job application portal via the 'Apply now' link on the official scholarship page
Nominate up to 2 research areas that best match your studies
The New Zealand Space Agency undertakes pre-selection of candidates before providing a final shortlist to JPL for consideration; up to seven graduate students may be selected
official.application_route: Apply online via the 'Apply now' link on the official MBIE scholarship page, which opens the Ministry's job application portal (requisition 20205); MBIE pre-selects candidates and sends a final shortlist to JPL, which makes the final selection.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be New Zealand citizens (a NASA requirement) and be enrolled in a postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution; New Zealand citizenship is stipulated by NASA, not only by MBIE.
official.international_eligibility: Not open to international students. Applicants must be New Zealand citizens, and people who currently hold or have previously held citizenship in a country listed on NASA's Designated Countries List are not eligible to apply.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Postgraduate STEM qualification (science, engineering, technology, mathematics or computer science) at a New Zealand tertiary institution in a field relevant to NASA's mission priorities; applicants nominate up to 2 research areas from the published list, which includes astrophysics and space science, astrobiology and biology, autonomy and robotics, planetary science, Earth observation and Earth science, instrument and sensor development, deep space communications, AI, machine learning and advanced computing, advanced aviation, and science and space communication. Only the New Zealand Space Agency at MBIE can accept applications for consideration by JPL.
official.duration: 3-month (up to 13 weeks) internship at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, July to September 2027 (dates subject to change)
official.description: The New Zealand Space Scholarship gives postgraduate STEM students the opportunity to undertake a fully supported 3-month internship at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, working alongside leading scientists and engineers on cutting-edge space missions and research. The initiative seeks to better prepare students for future careers in the New Zealand space and advanced aviation sectors; the New Zealand Space Agency at MBIE is the only official entity able to accept applications for consideration by JPL, and up to seven graduate students may be selected.
official.region: Oceania (New Zealand candidates); internship based at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Southern California, USA
official.program_type: Fully supported 3-month postgraduate internship at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (not a degree scholarship)
official.english_requirement: Applicants must be proficient in written and spoken English (NASA requirement); no IELTS, TOEFL or MOI test score is published

not_confirmed: value of the daily living allowance
verification.notes: Verified against the awarding body's own pages: the MBIE New Zealand Space Scholarship page (last updated 01 October 2026) and MBIE's official job application portal for requisition 20205 (posted 25/09/2026), which supplied the 1 November 2026 deadline, the up-to-seven-selection figure and the application route. Neither page publishes any monetary amount, so funding_amount, funding_currency and funding_period are recorded as null rather than estimated.

applicant_utility.summary: MBIE pays for return economy flights, accommodation near JPL, a daily living allowance and approved extra travel costs, but it never publishes what the allowance is worth, so budget for the gap. Applications for the 2027 round opened on 1 October 2026 and shut on 1 November 2026, giving candidates roughly a month. Up to seven graduate students are selected, and MBIE only pre-screens - JPL has the final say, so your application has to convince a NASA research centre that your work maps onto current JPL projects. You must be a New Zealand citizen and enrolled in postgraduate STEM study at a New Zealand tertiary institution in 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: New Zealand citizen postgraduate STEM students with strong grades (3.0+ on the US 4.0 scale) whose thesis or project lines up with JPL's mission areas and who can spend July to September 2027 in Southern California.
application_readiness_checklist: Convert your New Zealand grades to the US 4.0 GPA scale and confirm you meet the 3.0 minimum before starting, as NZ marks are not used directly
If you finish your current qualification in 2026, secure proof of 2027 postgraduate enrolment at a New Zealand tertiary institution, which must be provided before the scholarship is awarded
Register on MBIE's online job application portal early: the application portal is a separate account-based system, not a simple email form

Pick 1-2 research areas from the published list (for example autonomy and robotics, planetary science, Earth observation) that genuinely match your project, and align your answers to JPL's mission priorities
Check every citizenship you hold or have held against NASA's Designated Countries List (linked from the official page) before investing time in the application
Confirm you can be in person at JPL for July to September 2027 and can obtain a J1 or F1 visa plus travel and medical insurance
common_rejection_risks: Missing the single 1 November 2026 deadline - the round runs only about a month and late applications may not be considered
GPA below 3.0 once NZ grades are converted to the US 4.0 scale
A research area with weak relevance to JPL's active projects, since JPL makes the final selection from MBIE's shortlist
Current or former citizenship of a country on NASA's Designated Countries List, which excludes you outright under NASA's rules
Not being enrolled in postgraduate STEM study in 2027 at a New Zealand tertiary institution, or having no proof of enrolment
An incomplete portal application, since incomplete applications may not be considered
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The scholarship only covers costs associated with participating in the internship and explicitly leaves any additional expenses with the recipient, so expect to fund J1/F1 visa application costs, insurance beyond the support 'where applicable', and any personal spending not covered by the daily allowance; the value of that allowance is not published.
document_audit: No document checklist is published on either official page, so prepare a current academic record suitable for US GPA conversion, evidence of 2027 postgraduate enrolment, and identification covering citizenship before opening the portal application
The application itself is submitted through MBIE's account-based job application portal, which requires registration before you can complete requisition 20205
Only applications accepted through the Ministry's portal count - the Agency is the sole official route, so unsolicited direct contact with JPL will not put you in the pool
alerts: The window is unusually short: applications opened 1 October 2026 and closed 1 November 2026, so preparation has to happen before the round opens
MBIE only pre-selects; final selection is made by JPL, so a strong CV alone is not enough if your work does not map to JPL priorities
Internship dates (July to September 2027) are subject to change and must be attended in person in Southern California
NASA, not MBIE, imposes the citizenship, English-proficiency and Designated Countries List rules, and dual or former citizenships can disqualify you
Insurance and visa arrangements are the recipient's responsibility, and only 'reasonable travel-related expenses' including insurance support are reimbursed 'where applicable'
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on MBIE's online job application portal, complete the application for the 2027 New Zealand Space Scholarship (requisition 20205) including your nominated research areas, submit before the 1 November 2026 deadline, then wait for MBIE pre-selection and JPL's final decision.
